lower_bound.quote:
A nonnegative integer that
never increases and starts at a positive value can never reach \(0\); hence \(K\ge1\) at
every stage, so at least one nonunit remains at every stage.
lower_bound.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE: the integer sequence 1,0 is nonnegative, never increases, and starts positive, yet reaches 0. Thus monotonicity alone does not prove K≥1. The write-up needed to prove from the move formulas that every legal move leaves at least one of its two outputs greater than 1.
lower_bound.load_bearing: This is the stated justification that a terminal board cannot contain only 1s. Without it, the proof has established at most one terminal nonunit, but not exactly one.

parsed.notes: Mapping: lower_bound is part (a), using lexicographic descent plus nonunit survival; upper_bound is part (b), using primewise gcd invariance and unique factorization. Reduction is the valuation-level encoding of each move.
